# Reached cell boundary, advance DDA [S1]

The evidence explicitly states that the grid is traversed using the 3D digital differential analyzer (3D-DDA) algorithm. It further explains that when a non-empty cell is encountered, Woodcock tracking is performed. If a valid free-flight distance is found, traversal stops; otherwise, it continues to the next cell. This implies that the traversal logic involves reaching cell boundaries and advancing to the next cell (or stopping if a hit occurs), which aligns with the claim's description of reaching a cell boundary and advancing.
